title: Go: 100,000 and 1,000,000 rows
dataset: 10 columns per row: integers, strings (one unique per row), floats, a date/time and a boolean
method: Time and allocated bytes from go test -bench with the rows built beforehand and a discarding destination: about a dozen iterations per case at 100k rows (one for the in-memory case), three at 1M. Peak RSS from separate runs, one process per case, generating the rows on the fly; it includes the Go runtime and both libraries. Other processes were using the machine, so treat small differences as noise.
notes: The typed and struct-mapping cases make 27 to 66 allocations per workbook, whatever the number of rows.
With shared strings, memory grows with the number of distinct strings, here one per row.
The 1M-row file is 40.5 MB from Hypaxel and 62.9 MB from excelize's StreamWriter. At compression level 6 it is 29.0 MB and takes 1.32 s; at level 0 it is 331 MB and takes 0.37 s.
The in-memory excelize case was not run at 1M rows.
reproduce:
cd go/tests
go test -run '^$' -bench Write -benchmem                                 # 100,000 rows
go test -run '^$' -bench Write -benchmem -rows 1000000 -benchtime 3x     # 1,000,000 rows
go run ./cmd/bench                                                       # peak RSS, 100,000 rows
go run ./cmd/bench 1000000
